evidence: config/schemas/poses.schema.json: "parts": { "type": "array" } — no items schema (§5.3 CONFIRMED)

services/poses/poseEngine.js:77 and :178 read target.angleDeg; :185-186 reads target.continuous {direction, durationMs, speedPct=50}; :199-211 actuator uses target.direction/durationMs; :235-238 light uses target.action|state, brightness, durationMs

The validator is hand-written: services/schemaValidator.js supports type, enum, pattern, required, properties, items, anyOf, oneOf ONLY — there is no minimum/maximum/additionalProperties support (grep of lines 35-95)
items.remaining_work: Sketch: poses[].parts.items = object, required [partId, type, target], partId type [string,number], type enum [servo, linear_actuator, linear-actuator, light, led, motor], target oneOf: (a) required [angleDeg], angleDeg number; (b) required [continuous], continuous object required [direction,durationMs] with direction enum [cw,ccw,forward,reverse], speedPct number; (c) actuator: required [position] or [direction,durationMs]; (d) light: required one of action/state, state enum [on,off], brightness number. Numeric window checks (angleDeg within the calibrated window, partId exists, partId not blockAllMotion) CANNOT be expressed in this validator — add them as a gate step reusing services/poses/poseHealth.js (evaluatePoseHealth / annotatePoses / getPartSafetySummary, which already classify ok/degraded/blocked) rather than extending the JSON-schema engine.

items.name: Part-probe re-run spec (V11-HANDOFF §6) restated as ready-to-run — NOT run
evidence: routes/api/partsApi.js:202 `router.post('/:id/test', express.json(), ...)`; :213-214 resolves ctx via resolveCharacter(req) and passes { characterId: ctx.id } into the hardware call
services/characterContext.js:64-66 reads characterId from req.query and req.params ONLY — a characterId in the JSON BODY is silently ignored, so the probe MUST send it as a query string

services/hardwareService/exec.js:130-141 returns {status:'success', simulated:true} — but only when inTestMode AND CI==='true' AND !hardwareAvailable, so on a production node this specific flag is unlikely to fire; §6's framing of it as the main aliveness lie is only partly right
items.remaining_work: Ready-to-run spec: (1) For each candidate part, POST https://<owning-node>:3000/api/parts/<partId>/test?characterId=<N> (query param, NOT body; -k for the self-signed cert) from/against the node that OWNS the part — Orlok 192.168.8.120 char 3, Mina 192.168.8.140 char 2, Dragomir 192.168.8.130 char 4. (2) EXCLUDE 192.168.8.150 (PumpkinHead) and 192.168.8.200 (Groundbreaker) from the run entirely rather than letting their timeouts zero the results; Renfield (6) likewise. (3) Reject any response carrying simulated:true, and never score aliveness on a `success` field alone — require driver reach or observed motion, and grep /var/log/monsterbox.err on the node for the warn-only refusal reason after each call. (4) Safety exclusions, non-negotiable: Orlok parts 3, 4, 5 (candidates are 10, 15, and read-only checks on 1; 8 light is safe); Dragomir part 1 neck (candidates 2, 3 only); anything with blockAllMotion in config/hardware-safety.json; Mina parts 2 and 3 are hardware-dead so a null result there is expected, not a finding. (5) Do not re-probe Orlok part 14 — it is typed motion_sensor in parts.json yet carries an absolute-servo profile with a hand-set 12-180 window (still present, verified this session); that is a data fix, not a rig visit. (6) Read the three prior workflow journals under /home/remote/.claude/projects/-home-remote-MonsterBox/.../subagents/workflows/ before re-running.
